$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Fix this file, then regenerate. Every fact here is read from Microsoft's own pages, checked 2026-09-15: the Graph v1.0 subscription resource and its create/update/delete references, 'Receive change notifications through webhooks', 'Reduce missing change notifications', the identity-platform refresh-token page, and the Microsoft 365 Developer Program FAQ.
title: Microsoft Outlook

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Replaced but NOT revoked. Microsoft identity platform: "Refresh tokens replace themselves with a fresh token upon every use. The Microsoft identity platform doesn't revoke old refresh tokens when used to fetch new access tokens." So a retried or concurrent refresh cannot revoke the grant, which is the only thing the flag guards; the host persists whichever token came back last. Default lifetime 90 days.
oauth.$scopeComment: Calendars.Read is the least-privileged delegated permission Graph lists for subscribing to `event` and for reading events. offline_access is what makes the token response carry a refresh token at all. Application permissions (Calendars.Read as an app role) reach other users' mailboxes and are deliberately not what this connector asks for.
oauth.$comment: The package DECLARES the dance and does not perform it. `common` as the tenant accepts work, school and personal accounts; a host that serves one tenant may narrow it. Access tokens last about an hour, so a connection that is not refreshed stops working within the day -- which is why refreshToken is required rather than optional.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED 2026-09-15 against the Microsoft 365 Developer Program FAQ. A developer sandbox is a separate Microsoft 365 E5 TENANT with 25 users and sample calendar data, on the same graph.microsoft.com host -- so the credential is different and the URL is not. Eligibility is GATED: Visual Studio Professional/Enterprise subscribers, ISV Success Program / Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program members, or Premier/Unified Support customers; anyone else has no free sandbox. It lasts up to 90 days and renews only on development activity.
sandboxNote: Microsoft's test estate is a Microsoft 365 Developer Program sandbox: a separate E5 tenant with its own users, its own calendars and its own OAuth consent, on the SAME host. Eligibility is limited -- Visual Studio Professional or Enterprise subscribers, ISV Success / Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program members, or Premier/Unified Support customers -- and the tenant expires after 90 days of no development activity. Without one, every call reaches a real mailbox.

credentialFields.label: Application (client) ID
credentialFields.help: From the Microsoft Entra admin center -> App registrations. ONE value for the whole installation, not per connected account.

credentialFields.label: Client secret
credentialFields.help: A client secret of the same app registration. One value for the whole installation; Entra expires them, so record the expiry.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Microsoft account, and it expires after about ONE HOUR. The host refreshes it with the refresh token.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Microsoft account; issued only when the consent request includes offline_access. Every refresh answers with a NEW one -- persist it -- while the old one keeps working until it expires.

credentialFields.label: Client state
credentialFields.help: A secret the host chooses per connected account and sends as `clientState` on every subscription. Graph echoes it inside every notification, and that echo is the ONLY thing that authenticates a delivery -- Graph does not sign them. At most 128 characters.
